title: 2 Kings 14
paragraphs: ¹ In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah. ² He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem. ³ He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, though not as David his father had done — he followed the example of his father Joash. ⁴ Yet the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. ⁵ Once his hold on the kingdom was firm, he executed the officials who had assassinated his father.

⁶ But he did not put the murderers' children to death — for it was written in the Book of the Law of Moses that the LORD had commanded: fathers shall not die for what their children do, nor children for what their fathers do; each person must die for their own sin. ⁷ Amaziah struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and he captured Selah in battle, renaming it Joktheel — a name it still bears today. ⁸ Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, with a challenge: "Come, let us meet face to face on the battlefield." ⁹ Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah, "A thistle in Lebanon sent word to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' But a wild animal passing through trampled the thistle underfoot. ¹⁰ Yes, you've beaten Edom, and it's gone to your head. Enjoy your victory and stay home. Why stir up trouble that will only bring you down — and Judah with you?"

¹¹ But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash king of Israel marched out, and the two kings faced each other in battle at Bethshemesh in Judah. ¹² Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his own home. ¹³ Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah — the son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah — at Bethshemesh, then advanced on Jerusalem and broke down its wall from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, a stretch of four hundred cubits. ¹⁴ He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the LORD's temple and in the treasuries of the royal palace, along with hostages, and returned to Samaria. ¹⁵ The rest of the deeds of Jehoash — his might, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

¹⁶ Jehoash rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam succeeded him. ¹⁷ Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel. ¹⁸ The rest of the acts of Amaziah — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? ¹⁹ A conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish, but they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there. ²⁰ His body was brought back on horseback, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.

²¹ Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah. ²² He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after his father rested with his fathers. ²³ In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria and reigned for forty-one years. ²⁴ He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes — he did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin. ²⁵ He restored Israel's territory from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.

²⁶ For the LORD saw Israel's suffering — it was bitter indeed. There was no one left, slave or free, no one to help Israel. ²⁷ The LORD had not said he would blot out Israel's name from under heaven, so he saved them through the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash. ²⁸ The rest of the acts of Jeroboam — everything he did, his might in battle, how he recovered Damascus and Hamath for Israel — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? ²⁹ Jeroboam rested with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and his son Zachariah succeeded him.
